claims.text: A cluster normally runs its own DNS server; in Đơn Hàng's kind cluster it runs as Pods in kube-system behind the Service kube-dns, cluster IP 10.96.0.10, port 53 (53/UDP, 53/TCP, 9153/TCP).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods; outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/service-dns.txt

claims.text: The kubelet writes each container's /etc/resolv.conf with nameserver = the cluster DNS Service IP, so Pods (default dnsPolicy ClusterFirst) send lookups to the cluster DNS first.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods (Pod's DNS config; 'kubelet configures Pods' DNS'); Debugging DNS Resolution

claims.text: A Service with a cluster IP gets an A record <service>.<namespace>.svc.<cluster-domain> (cluster.local here) resolving to its cluster IP, not Pod IPs; web.svc.cluster.local and web.cluster.local are not Service names.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods (Services: A/AAAA records)

claims.text: A Pod in donhang has search domains donhang.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local; host search domains, if any, can be passed on through kind (node resolv.conf) and appear after these.
